paragraphs.text: 👑 PostQueen CLI and agent skill: schedule posts, upload media and read analytics from Claude Code, C
odex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw or any terminal.
postqueen is the command line for PostQueen: schedule posts, upload media and read analytics from a
terminal, a script or a coding agent.

Website ·
Docs ·
Pricing ·
npm
$0 due today. A card is required, and you pay nothing if you cancel within 7 days.
Posts you create with the CLI land on the same calendar you see in the PostQueen app.
## What it does
- Creates, lists, deletes and reschedules posts on the channels connected to your PostQueen workspac

e.
- Uploads images and videos and returns the path to use in a post.
- Reads channel analytics and

post analytics.
- Shows each channel's settings schema and runs its helper tools, such as Lemmy comm

unity search or Pinterest boards.
- Ships a skill and plugins, so coding agents such as Claude Code,
Cursor and Grok Build can run it for you.
## Quick start
You need Node.js 20.19 or newer (22.12 or newer on Node 22) and a PostQueen account. `postqueen auth
:login` opens PostQueen in your browser, a workspace admin approves the CLI, and it stores its own t
oken. On a machine with no browser, set `POSTQUEEN_API_KEY` to the key from Connections > API key in
stead. Only workspace admins can see the key, and each workspace has one.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Some networks need settings of their own before they accept a post. X, for example, needs `who_can_r
eply_post`. Run `postqueen integrations:settings <integration-id>` to see what a channel needs, and
pass it with `--settings '<json>'`.
No PostQueen account yet? Start a 7-day trial, $0 due today.
## Commands
| Command | What it does |
| `posts:create` | Create a post: `-c` content (repeat it for a thread or comments), `-s` date, `-i`
channel IDs, `-m` media paths, `-t draft` or `schedule`, `--settings`, or `--json <file>` for a ful

l request body |
| `posts:list` | List posts between two dates (30 days back to 30 days ahead by def

ault) |
| `posts:delete <id>` | Delete a post |
| `posts:status <id>` | Move a post between draft an

d scheduled |
| `posts:settings <id>` | Change the settings of a post that has not been published |

| `posts:missing <id>` | List recent content on the network for a post that has no release ID |
| `p

osts:connect <id>` | Connect a post to that content with `--release-id` |
| `integrations:list` | Li

st the connected channels |
| `integrations:groups` | List customer groups |
| `integrations:setting

s <id>` | Show a channel's settings schema and helper tools |
| `integrations:trigger <id> <method>`

| Run one of those helper tools, with `-d '<json>'` for its input |
| `analytics:platform <id>` | C

hannel analytics for the last 7 days, or `-d <days>` |
| `analytics:post <id>` | Analytics for one p

ost |
| `upload <file>` | Upload an image or video and get its path |
| `auth:status` | Check which

credentials the CLI uses and whether they work |
| `auth:login` | Sign in through your browser and s
tore a token. `--no-browser` prints the link instead of opening it. With `--auth-server` or `POSTQUE

EN_AUTH_SERVER`, log in through a device-flow auth server you run yourself |
| `auth:logout` | Remov
e the credentials `auth:login` stored |
Media goes in two steps: `upload` returns a `path`, and that path goes into `posts:create -m`. The c
ommand reference has every flag.

fails, the error goes to stderr and the command exits with code 1. `auth:status` prints its message
error goes to stderr and the command exits with code 1. `auth:status` prints its messages to stdout.
## Agent skill and plugins
The skill in `skills/postqueen` teaches an agent to run the CLI. Every route except DeepSeek Harness
runs the CLI, so install it and sign it in once with `postqueen auth:login`, or set `POSTQUEEN_API_
KEY` where the agent runs. DeepSeek Harness connects over MCP and needs `POSTQUEEN_API_KEY`.
| Agent | Install |

| Any agent that reads the `skills` registry | `npx skills add GkhanKINAY/postqueen-agent` |
|  Open
Claw | `npm install -g postqueen`, `npx skills add GkhanKINAY/postqueen-agent`, then `postqueen auth

:login` on that machine, or give OpenClaw the key as `POSTQUEEN_API_KEY` in its secret settings |
|
Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add GkhanKINAY/postqueen-agent`, then `/plugin install postqueen

@postqueen-agent` |
|  Cursor | Clone this repository and link it into `~/.cursor/plugins/local/post

queen` (manifest in `.cursor-plugin`) |
|  Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.co

m/GkhanKINAY/postqueen-agent` |
|  Grok Build | `grok plugin marketplace add GkhanKINAY/postqueen-ag

ent`, then `grok plugin install postqueen --trust` |
| Qwen Code | `qwen extensions install GkhanKIN

AY/postqueen-agent:postqueen` |
| DeepSeek Harness | `dsh plugin --profile web add "github:GkhanKINA
Y/postqueen-agent#path:/plugins/dsh-postqueen"`. This one connects over MCP instead of the CLI; see
agent#path:/plugins/dsh-postqueen"`. This one connects over MCP instead of the CLI; see its README |
Prefer tool calls to shell commands? Many agents connect to PostQueen over MCP instead, by signing i
n or with the API key. See the MCP guide and the agents overview.
## Privacy and security

- Channels connect through each network's official OAuth sign-in where the network offers one.
- Som
e networks, such as Bluesky, Lemmy, WordPress and Nostr, need an app password, an account password o

r a key that you paste in.
- PostQueen stores these credentials so it can post for you, and replaces

them when you remove the channel.
- Your API key and the `auth:login` token give full access to the
workspace. Keep the key in an environment variable, not in your code, and never paste either into a

n agent's chat.
- Read the privacy policy, or delete your account.
**No PostQueen account yet?** The CLI posts through PostQueen Cloud: start a trial, run `postqueen a
uth:login`, and your terminal or coding agent can post.
